name: Ronda
title: Holidays in Ronda
intro: A white town split by a deep gorge and joined by a towering stone bridge. Here's what Ronda is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are warm and good for walking. July and August are very hot in the day, though cooler than Seville or Córdoba. Winter days can be sunny, but nights are cold up in the mountains.

things.name: Puente Nuevo
things.blurb: The famous bridge over the El Tajo gorge. Walk down the paths below it for the best view.

things.name: Casa del Rey Moro
things.blurb: Gardens and a long stairway cut through the rock down to the river. Lots of steps back up.

things.name: Arab Baths
things.blurb: Well-kept Moorish bathhouses in the old town, with a short film explaining how they worked.

things.name: Alameda del Tajo
things.blurb: A shady park with a balcony on the cliff edge and a playground.

things.name: Caminito del Rey
things.blurb: A spectacular cliff walkway about an hour away. Children must be at least eight.

things.name: Setenil de las Bodegas
things.blurb: A white village where houses are built right under the overhanging rock.

faqs.question: Is Ronda good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a short stay or as part of a road trip. The bridge and gorge wow children, and the old town is easy to walk. Keep a close eye on little ones near the viewpoints.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Two or three nights covers the town, the gorge and a day out to the Caminito del Rey or the white villages.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly to Málaga, then drive about an hour and three quarters into the mountains, or take a bus. Spain is in the EU, so British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Is Ronda a good base for the white villages?
faqs.answer: Yes. Villages like Setenil, Grazalema and Zahara de la Sierra are all within an easy drive, so hiring a car is worth it.
